name: Middle Chinese
notes: STRUCTURAL ANCESTRY NODE (not a modelled G2P target). Middle Chinese (c. 600 CE, Qieyun) is the ancestor of the modern Sinitic varieties and the SOURCE of the Sino-Xenic literary borrowings in Japanese (kango), Korean (hanja) and Vietnamese (Sino-Vietnamese). It exists so that the ancestry and phylogenetic-distance metrics of the modern varieties that reference it have a node to resolve to. It carries no grapheme table. Middle Chinese is written in Chinese characters, which a letter table cannot model; a table needs a cited reconstruction, the romanization it is written in and the sound value of each symbol.

sources.author: Pulleyblank, E. G.
